results.question: What is the first-line antibiotic, dose basis, and duration for acute otitis media in a child?
claims: Pain: Paracetamol 15 mg/kg per dose every 6 h as needed
Amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 5 days
Severe or <6 months: Amoxicillin–Clavulanate 40 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component)
Mastoid tenderness, facial palsy, failure after 48–72 h of antibiotics
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-PED-01 v2024.1 (effective 2024-05-01) — Acute Otitis Media — Child OPD

results.question: A 6-year-old with non-severe community pneumonia: what is the amoxicillin dose exactly as the workflow states it? (Dose question — retrieve and cite the text as written; do not compute for any specific child.)
claims: Fever: Paracetamol 15 mg/kg per dose every 6 h as needed
Amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 5 days
No cough syrups under 5 years; no routine chest X-ray in OPD non-severe cases
Fast breathing for age without danger signs = non-severe pneumonia
Any danger sign (unable to drink, convulsions, chest indrawing) = REFER
Reassess at 48–72 h; no improvement = referral
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-PED-02 v2023.2 (effective 2023-11-01) — Community Pneumonia — Child OPD (Non-severe)

results.question: What is the first-line initial drug therapy for newly diagnosed adult hypertension? (Note: the pack may contain more than one edition of this workflow.)
claims: Uncontrolled at 4 weeks: combine Amlodipine + Telmisartan
Add Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg if still uncontrolled
Start Amlodipine 5 mg once daily OR Telmisartan 40 mg once daily
Resistant HTN on 3 drugs; suspected secondary cause; pregnancy
Baseline: creatinine, potassium, lipids, ECG, urine albumin
Two readings, two occasions; rule out secondary causes if <30 y
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-GP-02 v2025.2 (effective 2025-06-01) — Hypertension — Initial Management (Adult)

results.question: Which analgesic class must be avoided in suspected dengue, and why?
claims: AVOID Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Aspirin and all NSAIDs — bleeding risk
Fever + two of: headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, rash, leukopenia
Paracetamol 500–650 mg every 6 h for fever (max 3 g/day); adequate oral fluids
Daily CBC from day 3 of illness
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-GP-04 v2024.2 (effective 2024-07-01) — Dengue Fever — OPD Management

results.question: What are the ORS volumes after each loose stool for a child aged 2–10 years, and what zinc course accompanies it?
claims: ORS after every loose stool: 50–100 ml (<2 y), 100–200 ml (2–10 y)
Zinc 20 mg once daily for 14 days (10 mg if <6 months)
Continue feeding; ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg single dose only for persistent vomiting
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-PED-03 v2024.1 (effective 2024-03-01) — Acute Gastroenteritis — Child OPD

results.question: Which red flags in acute low back pain mandate imaging or referral?
claims: Fever with spinal tenderness; significant trauma; age >65 with new pain + weight loss
Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel involvement, progressive weakness
Reassess at 2 weeks; persistent >6 weeks = imaging pathway
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-ORT-01 v2023.1 (effective 2023-09-01) — Acute Low Back Pain — Adult OPD

results.question: Which urinary antibiotic is avoided at 36+ weeks of pregnancy, and what is the stated alternative?
claims: Nitrofurantoin near term (36+ weeks)
Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days (avoid at 36+ weeks)
Ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones throughout pregnancy
Alternative: Cefixime 200 mg twice daily for 5 days
Dysuria/frequency; urine routine + culture before antibiotics where possible
Repeat culture after treatment (test of cure)
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-GYN-02 v2023.1 (effective 2023-06-01) — Urinary Tract Infection in Pregnancy

results.question: At what HbA1c threshold at diagnosis does the workflow add a second agent to metformin, and which agent?
claims: HbA1c ≥8.5% at diagnosis: add Glimepiride 1 mg before breakfast
HbA1c every 3 months until at goal; annual creatinine and urine albumin
Metformin 500 mg once daily with dinner; up-titrate weekly to 500 mg twice daily as tolerated
FPG ≥126 mg/dL or HbA1c ≥6.5% on two occasions, or RPG ≥200 with symptoms
labels: NATIONAL STW STW-GP-03 v2024.1 (effective 2024-09-01) — Type 2 Diabetes — Diagnosis & Initiation

results.question: What is the first-line prophylactic drug for migraine in adults?
What is the standard drug regimen for newly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis?
Per the clinic's own protocol, when are empirical antibiotics started in adult acute undifferentiated fever — and does the national workflow pack say the same? Label your sources.
claims: Day 2: if fever persists beyond 48 hours without a localizing source, start empirical Azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days.
Documentation: record fever chart and medication reconciliation at each visit.
Day 0–1: Paracetamol per standard reference dosing; hydration advice; CBC + peripheral smear if fever > 48h; dengue NS1 in season.
Day 3–4: review with reports; escalate per findings; admit if warning signs.
labels: CLINIC PROTOCOL (Sunrise Multi-speciality Clinic, SOP-CLIN-014 v2.1, approved 2026-03-10) — organization-level knowledge, not national guidance
